options: The physical size of a table on disk
Maintaining the level of details in a table
The number of users who can query a table
The encryption applied to a column
The order in which rows are stored
questions.explanation: Data Cardinality is about maintaining the level of details in a table, and understanding it is said to solve 90% of data problems.

options: When a table has a high number of duplicates
When a table has many columns
When there are no or few duplicates in a table
When a table has many foreign keys
When a table is very large
questions.explanation: High Cardinality is when there are no or few duplicates in a table; tables with a primary key are mostly in highest cardinality mode.

questions.stem: Which kind of table is mostly in Low Cardinality mode?
options: Tables with a primary key
Tables with a foreign key
Empty tables
Lookup tables
Temporary tables
questions.explanation: Low Cardinality is when there is a high number of duplicates, and tables with foreign keys are mostly in Low Cardinality mode.

questions.stem: In the Product and Sales example, why does the Sales table have Low Cardinality with respect to Products?
options: Because it has no primary key
Because Product names are stored in it
Because it stores fewer rows than the Product table
Because Sales rows are deleted daily
Because one product can be sold many times, so Product ID repeats across many rows
questions.explanation: One type of product can be sold many times, so the Sales table holds thousands of rows with repeated Product IDs.

questions.stem: On what basic concept is normalisation said to depend?
options: Encryption
Compression
Indexing
Partitioning
Cardinality
questions.explanation: The basic concept of normalisation is dependent on Cardinality; breaking denormalised tables apart leaves the main table with High Cardinality data.

questions.stem: Why can we NOT say that all primary key tables have absolute highest cardinality?
options: Because primary keys can be null
Because cardinality only applies to fact tables
Because primary keys are only used in OLAP
Because tables with a foreign key can also have a primary key and become the primary table for another foreign key table
Because duplicates are always allowed in primary tables
questions.explanation: A table holding a foreign key can also carry its own primary key and act as the primary table for yet another table, so absolute highest cardinality cannot be assumed.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the three degrees of cardinality?
options: One to One (1:1)
One to Many (1:M)
Many to Many (M:N)
Many to None (M:0)
All of these are degrees of cardinality
questions.explanation: The three degrees are One to One, One to Many and Many to Many; 'Many to None' is not a degree of cardinality.

questions.stem: What does a One to Many (1:M) relationship mean?
options: A single row in table A relates to many rows in table B
A single row in table A relates to a single row in table B
Many rows in table A relate to many rows in table B
Table A has no relationship with table B
Table A and table B are the same table
questions.explanation: One to Many means a single row in table A relates to many rows in table B.

questions.stem: What can happen when tables are joined using the wrong columns, without direct primary and foreign key relationships?
options: The query runs faster
The result is automatically deduplicated
The result can end up as Cartesian data
Cardinality increases
Foreign keys are created automatically
questions.explanation: Joining with no direct Pkey and Fkey relationship, or using wrong columns, can end up in Cartesian data.

questions.stem: When a table structure changes for a business requirement, what is the first question to ask, and what helps trace the impact?
options: Whether the change affects cardinality; Data Lineage, backed by Metadata Management, shows the end-to-end impact
Whether the change affects disk space; the DBA shows the impact
Whether the change affects colour schemes; the BI tool shows the impact
Whether the change affects licensing; the vendor shows the impact
Whether the change affects network load; the firewall shows the impact
questions.explanation: The first question is whether the change impacts the cardinality of any table; if so, Data Lineage, which needs Metadata Management in place, shows the end-to-end impact.
